chief_complaint: painless bright red blood dripping after bowel movement
hpi_details: A 38-year-old female presents to the clinic with painless bright red blood dripping after bowel movement. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks she tore a small blood vessel or scratched herself inside from straining during recent hard bowel movements.
concerns: She is worried that the bleeding is a sign of bowel cancer like the kind that took her mother's life.
expectations: She hopes to receive a soothing prescription cream or suppository to stop the bleeding and avoid an invasive colonoscopy.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Internal Hemorrhoids (bleeding) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management for Internal Hemorrhoids (bleeding) emphasizes a high-fiber diet, stool softeners, and topical hydrocortisone, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

teaching.one_liner: Dilated veins of the internal hemorrhoidal plexus causing painless bright red bleeding, typically noticed on the toilet paper or coating the stool.
red_flags: Weight loss or change in bowel habits accompanying the bleeding — needs colon cancer workup, especially over age 45-50

must_ask.say: Is the bleeding painful, or completely painless?
Is the blood bright red, and does it drip after a bowel movement or mix into the stool?
How long has this been happening, and how often?
Any unintentional weight loss or change in your bowel habits?
Do you strain or have hard stools?

history.answer: I came in because I noticed bright red blood dripping into the toilet bowl after my bowel movements.
It is bright, fresh red blood, not dark red and definitely not black like tar.
The blood drips directly into the toilet water after the stool passes, and I also see bright red blood on the toilet paper when I wipe.
It began about two weeks ago and has been happening more frequently over the past several days.
It happens almost every time I go to the bathroom, dripping several drops into the water each time.
No, there is no pain at all when the stool passes or when it bleeds.
I sometimes feel a small soft swelling around the anus after straining, but it goes back inside on its own.
I feel mild moisture and occasional itching around the area, but there is no foul drainage or discharge.
Yes, my stools are frequently hard and dry, and I usually have to sit and strain for ten to fifteen minutes.
No, I still go once every one to two days, but the consistency has just been harder than usual.
My stools are normal caliber, not thin like a pencil, and I do not have a feeling of incomplete emptying afterward.
No, I do not have any abdominal pain, cramps, or stomach discomfort.
No, I have not had any loose watery stools or mucus mixed with my bowel movements.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or night sweats.
I felt slightly lightheaded when I stood up quickly yesterday, but I have not had dizziness spells or blackouts.
Yes, I have been feeling unusually run down and fatigued lately, especially over the past week.
No, my weight has remained completely stable.
No, I have not had any indigestion, stomach burning, nausea, or vomiting of blood.
No, I have not eaten beets, blueberries, or blood sausage recently, and I do not take iron supplements.
I have never had a colonoscopy or any other bowel scope before.
I thought maybe I just tore something or scratched the inside while straining to pass a hard stool.
I'm really terrified that this blood in the toilet could be bowel cancer, because my mother passed away from that.
I was hoping you could give me a soothing cream or suppository to stop the bleeding so I don't have to undergo a colonoscopy.
I do not have any chronic medical problems like high blood pressure, diabetes, or liver disease.
I have never had any surgeries and I have never been hospitalized.
I do not take any prescription medications, aspirin, blood thinners, or over-the-counter pain relievers.
I have no known allergies to any medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes.
I only drink a glass of wine socially once or twice a month.
I work in an office sitting at a desk for most of the day, and I live with my husband.
No one in my family has had colorectal cancer, polyps, or inflammatory bowel disease.
My last period started two weeks ago and my cycles are regular; there is no chance that I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 115/75 mmHg, pulse 78 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 36.7 C, and oxygen saturation 99% on ambient air.
No significant drop in systolic blood pressure or excessive compensatory tachycardia upon standing from a seated position.
Mild conjunctival pallor noted bilaterally; sclerae are non-icteric without injection.
Abdomen is flat and symmetric without surgical scars, distension, or visible peristalsis.
Normoactive bowel sounds heard in all four quadrants; no bruits auscultated over the aorta or renal vessels.
Abdomen is soft, non-distended, and completely non-tender without palpable masses, guarding, or organomegaly.

Perianal inspection reveals no external fissure, skin tags, or thrombosed external hemorrhoids; digital examination notes normal sphincter tone, no palpable rectal masses, and trace bright red blood on the examining glove with soft brown stool.
